A “Setu” coin with a bull on the obverse: “Setu” warijɛ dɔ, misi dɔ bɛ a ɲɛfɛ. Setu daɲɛ — Lanka ka dancɛ, Rameswaram — bɛ sɔrɔ Jaffna masaya cɛmancɛla waati labanw Tamil faamaw ka warijɛw kan; couchant bull, Shiva’s Nandi, o ye u ka minɛn ye min bɛ kɛ ɲɔgɔn fɛ.
A burial urn of the kind that made Adich: Sudon-minɛn sugu min ye Adichanallur tɔgɔ Bɔ. Suw — walima u kolo lajɛlenw — tun bɛ bila o bɔgɔdaga suguw kɔnɔ ni kaburufɛnw ye, ka su don kabakurunw kɔnɔ Thamirabarani sanfɛ. Urnw ye ɲɔgɔndan tilennen ye ni Sangam poyi முதுமக்கள் தாழி ye.
A catalogue of the coins issued by the C: Chera, Chola ani Pandya masakɛw ye warijɛ minnu bɔ, n’u ka masakɛ taamasiyɛnw ye, n’olu ye bow, tiger ani jɛgɛ ye, olu ka gafesɛbɛn.
A ceramic vessel from Adichanallur. Smal: Seramiki minɛn dɔ bɔra Adichanallur. Nin daga misɛnninw tun bɛ bila sudon dagaw kɔnɔ walima u kɛrɛfɛ, laala dumuni, ji walima sarakaw tun bɛ u kɔnɔ suw ye — nɛgɛ waati dannaya jiracogo dɔ, min tun bɛ taama na min bɛ tɛmɛ saya kan.
A chariot for a creeper, a shawl for a p: Wotoro bɛ kɛ jirisunba ye, sɔgɔli bɛ kɛ wulu ye, jiriden min bɛ ɲɛnamaya di poyikɛla ma : patɔrɔnw ka nilifɛn tɔgɔba dɔw bɛ i n’a fɔ u tɛ se ka kɛ, wa o de y’u ka kuma ye. Kodai madam ye bolomafara ye min ka ca fo a dibaga tɛ jatebɔ kɛ nilifɛn in baaracogo la — hinɛ bɛ se baganw, jiriw ani kalan ma.
A Chera coin in the collection of the Na: Chera warijɛ dɔ min bɛ Napier misiri ka fɛnw lajɛlen na, Thiruvananthapuram. Chera warijɛw bɛ ni bɛlɛkisɛ ni bɛlɛkisɛ ye, o min ye masadugu taamasiyɛn ye, wa misali fɔlɔ caman bɛ bɔ Karur, Chera santiri min bɛ Amaravathi kan.
A chieftain of the Ay line in the southe: Ay layini kuntigi dɔ min bɛ Podiyil (Pothigai) kulu jamana saheliyanfan na. Laada lakodɔnnen dɔ bɛ a ka fini nafama dɔ di ala dɔ ma, min bɛ fɔ tuma caman na ko Shiva — ka di i n’a fɔ yɛrɛdi ka fara bolomafara kan.
A chieftain of the Malaiyaman lineage, o: Malaiyaman bɔnsɔn kuntigi dɔ, jamana lamini Mullur ni Tirukkoyilur, hakili jigira a ka munificence la poyikɛlaw ma ani mɔgɔ bɛɛ ma minnu nana a fɛ. A jɔyɔrɔ tun bɛ patɔrɔn wolonwula cɛma, o b’a jira ko faama dɔ bonya tun bɛ suman a ka nili fɛ i n’a fɔ a ka waajulikɛyɔrɔ.
A Chola coin carrying Pandya royal insig: Chola warijɛ dɔ min tun bɛ ni Pandya masakɛ taamasiyɛnw ye. Tuma min na Cholaw ye Pandya jamana don u ka fanga kɔrɔ, u ye Pandya jɛgɛ bila u yɛrɛ ka waraba kɛrɛfɛ — se sɔrɔli taamasyɛn min gosira nɛgɛ la.
A city where literature, royal patronage: Dugu min kɔnɔ sɛbɛnniw, masakɛw ka dɛmɛ, diinɛ ani duguba kɔnɔ ɲɛnamaya ye ɲɔgɔn sɔrɔ kabini san ba fila ɲɔgɔn.
A coin of Kulottunga Chola bearing the t: Kulottunga Chola ka warijɛ dɔ min tɔgɔ ye ko “Malai Nadu konda Chola” — Chola min ye kulu jamana ta, o kɔrɔ ye ko Chera dugukolo. Chola masakɛw y’u ka se sɔrɔli weleweleda tɔgɔw la minnu tun bɛ u ka warijɛw kan ka fara u ka sɛbɛnniw kan.
A coin of Kulottunga I (1070–1120 CE), w: Kulottunga I (1070–1120 K.Ɲ.) ka warijɛ dɔ, min ye Chola ni kɔrɔnfɛ Chalukya layiniw fara ɲɔgɔn kan ani ka Chola masaya jan ni ɲɛtaa dɔ mara. A ka warijɛw bɛ Tɛmɛ Chola suguya sabatilenw kan n’a tɔgɔ ye Nagarikan na.
A coin of Rajaraja I. His copper coins o: Rajaraja I ka warijɛ dɔ A ka nɛgɛ warijɛ minnu ye masakɛ jɔlen ni sigilan suguya ye, minnu donna a ka Sri Lanka worodugu minɛni kɔfɛ, olu tun bɛ jɛnsɛn kosɛbɛ kɔgɔji fan fila bɛɛ la, wa u ladege kɛra san kɛmɛ caman kɔnɔ.
A coin of the Jaffna kingdom showing a h: Jafna masaya warijɛ dɔ min bɛ sow jira ni jɛgɛ ye. Jaffna Tamil masakɛw (san kɛmɛda 13nan–17nan) ye warijɛw bɔ Ɛndujamana Saheli laada la, o min ye hakilijigin ye jɛɲɔgɔnya gɛlɛnw na Palk Strait cɛ.
A coin of the Kongu Cheras, the Chera li: Kongu Cheras ka warijɛ dɔ, Chera layini min ye Kongu jamana mara Tamil tlebi mara la (bi Coimbatore, Erode ani Karur lamini na) — o mara kelen min ye Romɛ warijɛ marayɔrɔ nafamaw sɔrɔ.
A crowned, moustached figure in profile,: Ja dɔ min bɛ ni masafugulan ye, a kunsigi bɛ a ɲɛda la, a bɛ jakite don min dilalen don ni kabakurunw ye ani a bɛ ni fulakɛw ye minnu bɛ woyo, o bɛ bere dɔ kɔrɔta min kuncɛ ye wuluwulu ye. Ɲɛda ni bolow jalen don ni tigɛli nɛrɛmuguma ɲuman ye dugukolo jɛman kan ani finiw kolen don ni ochre, pink ani green ye — o ye ja ye min bɛ i n’a fɔ masaso finidoncogo kalan ye batoso ja dɔ kɔnɔ.
A detail of the painted ceiling of the J: Jainw ka kuluba batoso sanfɛla pentalen dɔ ɲɛfɔlen don Sittanavasal: lotus pinki minnu bɛ da wuli pads verts cɛma, bagan dɔ bɛ ka wuli ji kɔnɔ ani ja dɔ bɛ ka falenfɛnw lajɛ. Tuma caman na, o jidagayɔrɔ bɛ kalan iko samavasarana ka lotus moat, sankolo lajɛ min na Jain Tirthankara bɛ waajuli kɛ yɔrɔ min na, ni kantigiw bɛ falenfɛnw lajɛ ka di.
A funerary vessel from the burial cairns: Sukununi minɛn dɔ bɔra Nilgiri kuluw sudon yɔrɔw la, a datugulan kunbere bɛ ni ja misaliw ye. San kɛmɛ tan ni kɔnɔntɔnnan na, Nilgiri kuluw sɛgɛsɛgɛlikɛlaw ye o ɲɔgɔnna datugulan caman sɔrɔ minnu sanfɛ, mɔgɔw, baganw ani sotigiw — ja misɛnninw bɔgɔ la minnu bɛ se ka suw ka ɲɛnamaya n’u jɔyɔrɔ jira.
A garland of about a hundred and fifty a: Garland min bɛ akam vɛrɛsi kɛmɛ ni bi duuru ɲɔgɔn bɔ Kanimethaviyar fɛ, dɔw bɛ se ka kɛ bi saba ye dugukolo ja duuru kelen-kelen bɛɛ kama.
A gold coin of Rajaraja I (985–1014 CE),: Rajaraja I (985–1014 K.Ɲ.) ka sanu warijɛ dɔ, min ye batoso belebele jɔ Thanjavur. A bɛ Chola masakɛ taamasiyɛn kɔrɔ jira: jara sigilen min bɛ Pandya jɛgɛ fila kɛrɛfɛ, yɛrɛmahɔrɔnya parasol jukɔrɔ, ni masakɛ tɔgɔ ye Nagarikan na — Cholaw b’a fɔ k’u bɛ saheli mara.
A gold half-kahavanu of Virarajendra Cho: Virarajendra Chola (1063–1070 K.Ɲ.) ka sanu tilancɛ kahavanu dɔ. Kahavanu (ka bɔ kahapana la) tun ye sanu diinɛ ye Sri Lanka, ani Chola sanu min gosira ka kɛɲɛ ni o sariya ye, o bɛ Chola ka mara waati jira gun in kan.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Kadiya: Kadiyalur Uruthirankannanar ka poyi ɲɛminɛbaga dɔ min bɛ wele ko Idylls tan. Bard dɔ min ka yazh ka bon, o bɛ bilasira ka taa Thondaiman Ilanthiraiyan fɛ Kanchi; sira kan, poyi in bɛ duguw, kurunbonkarilaw ani mɔgɔw ka ɲɛjirali ɲɛnamaw jira.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Mudath: Mudathama Kanniyar ka poyi ɲɛminɛbaga dɔ min bɛ Idylls tan kan. Dununfɔla dɔ (porunar) min ye sara caman sɔrɔ, o bɛ a barokɛɲɔgɔn dɔ bilasira ka taa Chola masakɛ bolomafara Karikal Valavan fɛ.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Nallur: Nallur Nathathanar ka poyi ɲɛminɛbaga dɔ min bɛ Idylls tan kan. Bard min bɛ yazh (harp) fitinin fɔ, o bɛ dɔ wɛrɛ bila ka taa kuntigi Nalliyakkodan fɛ, ka bard faantanw ka gɛlɛyaw ɲɛfɔ ani patɔrɔn bolomafara dɔ ka dusu suma.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Perunk: Idili tan ka poyi ɲɛminɛbaga dɔ min sɛbɛnna Perunkausikanar fɛ. Yaala-yaalakɛlaw (koothar) bɛ bilasira ka taa kuntigi Nannan fɛ; poyi in bɛ seli kɛ kuluw mankan caman minɛni kosɔn .
A large storage jar associated with Adic: Fɛnmarayɔrɔba dɔ min ni Adichanallur bɛ tali kɛ ɲɔgɔn na. Suman, ji ani dumuni wɛrɛw tun bɛ daga minnu kɔnɔ; sudon yɔrɔw la, minɛn minnu bonya bɛ nin cogo la, olu fana tun bɛ se ka kɛ dagaw ye. Daɲɛ “dolio” bɛ mɔgɔ hakili jigin dolium la, o min tun ye Romɛkaw ka diɲɛ kɔnɔ fɛn marayɔrɔba ye.
A large, round-bellied funerary urn from: Sukununikɛlan belebeleba dɔ, kɔnɔbara lamininen don, ka bɔ Adichanallur. Nin bɔgɔdaga suguw tun bɛ se ka jɔ ka janya ka tɛmɛ denmisɛnnin kan, wa u kɛli tun bɛ sekoba de wajibiya: Sangam poyikɛlaw bɛ kuma bɔgɔdagakɛla fɛ min ye dagaw dilan i n’a fɔ கலம்செய் கோவே — “E bɔgɔdagakɛlaw cɛma masakɛ”.
A lead coin from Andipatti bearing a leg: Plɔmu warijɛ dɔ bɔra Andipatti min kɔnɔ, nsiirin dɔ bɛ Tamil-Brahmikan na. Masakɛ saba minnu tun bɛ masafugulan don u la, Sangam waati sigida kuntigiw tun bɛ warijɛ bɔ ni plɔmu ni nɛgɛ ye, wa Tamil-Brahmi nsiirin minnu bɛ u kan, olu bɛ dɛmɛ ka tɔgɔw da o faamaw ma.
A line drawing of the vimana and a pilla: Vimana ni Brihadisvara batoso ka so jɔlen dɔ ja.
A love poem of the Ten Idylls by Kapilar: Kapilar ka Idylls tan ka kanuya poyi dɔ, min sigilen bɛ kulu (kurinji) jamana kɔnɔ. Laada b’a fɔ ko a sɛbɛnna walasa ka worodugu masakɛ dɔ kalan Tamil kanuya poyi cɛɲi na; a tɔgɔ bɔra kosɛbɛ ka falen bi kɔnɔntɔn ni kɔnɔntɔn tɔgɔ da.
A modern artist’s imagining of a busy ha: Bi dɔnkotigi dɔ ka miirili kurunw, suguw ani sankansobaw ka kurunbonkariyɔrɔ la min falen bɛ mɔgɔw la, ɲɛfɔliw kɔfɛ Silappathikaram ani Pattinappalai kɔnɔ. O tɛ dalilu ye min b’a jira ko dugu tun bɛ cogo min na tiɲɛ na.
A modern sketch imagining ships and buil: Bi ja dɔ min bɛ kurunw ni sow miiri kurunbonkariyɔrɔ kɔrɔ la. I n’a fɔ Puhar jɔli kura bɛɛ, a bɛ sɛbɛnni ɲɛfɔliw kɔrɔ fɔ; kurunbonkarila in labɛncogo dafalen tɛ dɔn.
A name linked with Nedunalvadai and Tiru: Tɔgɔ min ni Nedunalvadai ani Tirumurukarruppatai bɛ tali kɛ ɲɔgɔn na Idylls tan kɔnɔ — hali n’a bɛ se ka kɛ poyikɛla caman ta ye waati danfaralenw kɔnɔ. Kɔfɛ nsiirinw b’a fɔ a ka ban k’a ka kiritigɛ di poyi dɔ ma hali Shiva ma Pandya ka kiritigɛso la: hakili jagɛlɛya taamasyɛn, tariku ko tɛ.
A Note on the Evidence: Kɔlɔsili dɔ min kɛra daliluw kan
A palm-leaf manuscript from the museum’s: Bololasɛbɛn min dilalen don ni jiribulu ye, o bɔra mise ka fɛnw lajɛlen na.
A Pandya coin of the “massa” type. Massa: Pandya warijɛ dɔ min ye “massa” suguya ye. Massa ye tɔgɔ ye min bɛ di cɛmancɛla waati nɛgɛ warijɛw ma min bɛ ja jɔlen jira fan kelen fɛ ani ja sigilen jira fan dɔ fɛ — suguya min jɛnsɛnna Cholas fɛ ani min tɛmɛna Pandyaw fɛ ani Sri Lanka masakɛw fɛ.
A Pandya coin showing a standing king wi: Pandya warijɛ dɔ min bɛ masakɛ jɔlen dɔ jira ni jɛgɛ taamasiyɛn ye. Faama jɔlen dɔ ja, min tun bɛ dɔn Chola nɛgɛ warijɛ fɛ, o minɛna Pandyas fɛ tuma min na u ka fanga seginna a cogo kɔrɔ la san kɛmɛda 13nan na.
A Pandya coin with the twin fish and a b: Pandya warijɛ dɔ ni jɛgɛ filaninw ni misiden dɔ. Jɛgɛ fila-fila kɛra Pandya taamasiyɛn ye min bɛ to senna, min jalen don poyiw ka Madurai pankartiw kan, ka gosi warijɛw kan san ba kelen ni kɔ kɔnɔ.
A pillared hall today: Salon min ye pilan ye bi
A pipeline of terracotta rings, set one: Terakota bololanɛgɛw pibiliki dɔ, min bilalen bɛ kelen sanfɛ ɲɔgɔn sanfɛ sankanso naani kɔnɔ, o bɔra kɛnɛ kan Korkai sɛgɛsɛgɛli la. Bɔgɔdaga tasumabɔlenw ni kɔlɔnw i n’a fɔ nin, olu tun bɛ ji ta ani k’a ji bɔ tariku Tamil jamana fɔlɔ duguw kɔnɔ — o ye don o don injiniyɛri dɔ ye min bɛ kɛ kurunbonkarila dɔ la min falen bɛ mɔgɔw la.
A poem of the Ten Idylls by Kadiyalur Ur: Kadiyalur Uruthirankannanar ka Idylls tan poyi dɔ, min bɛ Chola masakɛ Karikal Valavan tanu ani a ka kurunbonkari dugu min falen bɛ mɔgɔw la, n’o ye Kaveripoompattinam (Puhar) ye, n’a ka kurunw, suguw ani seliw.
A poem of the Ten Idylls by Nakkeerar. D: Idyll tan ka poyi dɔ min sɛbɛnna Nakkeerar fɛ. Worodugu fiɲɛ jan ni nɛnɛba waati la, nɛnɛ waati, masamuso dɔ b’a cɛ nege don a la k’a sɔrɔ masakɛ b’a ka sɔrɔdasi joginlenw ladon kɛlɛyɔrɔ dɔ la.
A portrait coin of the Chera king Kuttuv: Chera masakɛ Kuttuvan Kotai ja warijɛ dɔ, a tɔgɔ dara Tamil-Brahmikan na. Makkotai warijɛw fɛ, nin warijɛ bɔko minnu man ca — n’a sɔrɔla olu lawulila Romɛkaw ka ja warijɛw fɛ minnu bɛ na jago fɛ — olu bɛ Ɛndu warijɛ fɔlɔw cɛma walasa ka faama ɲɛda jira.
A potsherd inscribed in Tamil-Brahmi, fo: Bɔgɔdaga dɔ min sɛbɛnnen bɛ Tamil-Brahmikan na, o sɔrɔla Tissamaharama la Sri Lanka saheliyanfan fɛ, wa a kɛra san kɛmɛ 2nan ɲɔgɔn na Krisita tile ɲɛ. Sɛbɛnni Tamilkan na bɔgɔdaga kan min yɔrɔ ka jan Tamil jamanaba la, o b’a jira ko Tamil jagokɛlaw tun bɛ baara la kɔgɔji kɛrɛfɛ tariku waati daminɛ na.
A rare book from the first decades of Ta: Gafe min man ca, min bɔra Tamil sɛbɛnni san tan fɔlɔw la, waati min na sɛbɛn kɔrɔw minnu maralen bɛ jirisun buluw kan, olu tun bɛ ka bila sɛbɛnnikɛlan na a siɲɛ fɔlɔ la.
A rare volume digitised from CICT’s arch: Volume min man ca, o kɛra nizɛrikan na ka bɔ CICT ka sɛbɛnmarayɔrɔ la, ka mara walasa ka kalan kɛ. Katalogu kunnafoni dafalenw bɛna fara a kan mise ɲɛmɔgɔw fɛ.
A Sangam-age Chola coin with a tiger and: Sangam-age Chola warijɛ dɔ ni waraba ni waraba ye. Chola warijɛ fɔlɔw, minnu fanba ye nɛgɛ ye, olu sinsinnen bɛ jara kan — o taamasyɛn kelen min tun bɛna ta masakɛ Cholaw fɛ san ba kelen o kɔfɛ. Uraiyur ni Kaveripoompattinam tun ye u ka santiribaw ye.
A Sangam-age Pandya coin, typically a sm: Sangam waati Pandya warijɛ, a ka c’a la, nɛgɛso kɛnɛ fitinin min bɛ ni waraba ye a fan kelen fɛ, jɛgɛ min bɛ kɛ cogo la min bɛ kɛ fan dɔ fɛ. O warijɛ suguw tun bɛ yaala Madurai ani a lamini na, Pandya faaba min tun bɛ seli kɛ Maduraikkanchi.
A scholarly study of government, adminis: Dɔnnibaaw ka kalan dɔ kɛra gɔfɛrɛnaman, marako ani sigida ɲɛnamaya kan Tamil jamana na Sangam waati la.
A second coin of the Kongu Cheras. Compa: Kongu Cheras ka warijɛ filanan. Aw ye o fila suma ɲɔgɔn na: warijɛ minnu bɛ kɛ ni bolo ye, olu bɛ danfara bɔ u sɔgɔli la, u doncogo la ani u tigɛcogo la, wa o danfara suguw bɛ warijɛ dɔnbagaw dɛmɛ u ka koɲɛw ɲɛnabɔ ani ka warijɛw tora u la waati hakɛ min na.
A second image of the four-armed, seated: Ganesha bolo naani, sigilen ja filanan. Aw k’a hakɛw, a masirifɛnw ani a jirisunba jiginni suma ni fɔlɔ ye : Silpa Sastraw ka kanon jɛlen kɔnɔ, jagokɛla ni atelier bɛɛ y’a yɛrɛ ka magali to.
A selection drawn from the Thirukkural,: Sugandili min bɔra Thirukkural kɔnɔ, min bɛ kumasenw lajɛ minnu bɛ to mɔgɔ hakili la kalanbagaw ye.
A separate photographing of the opening: Ja danfaralen min bɛ bɔ bundle 579 D daminɛ buluw la, n’o ye Maduraikkanchi ye.
Shaiva senuma dɔ, bolow faralen ɲɔgɔn kan bato la. Chola masakɛw ye bonya da Nayanmar bi wɔɔrɔ ni saba kan, Sekkizhar ye minnu ka ɲɛnamaya fɔ Periya Puranam kɔnɔ, ani u ka nɛgɛ jaw tun bɛ sigi batosow kɔnɔ, ka taa ni u ye seli taamaw la.
A sherd illustrated in Vimala Begley’s 1: Sherd min jiralen bɛ Vimala Begley ka san 1983 sɛgɛsɛgɛli la min kɛra Arikamedu ka donko kan. Ka segin ka layini sɛgɛsɛgɛlenw sɛgɛsɛgɛ, Begley y’a jira ko sigili daminɛna san kɛmɛ sabanan cɛmancɛ lamini na Krisita tile ɲɛ — ka kɔn Mortimer Wheeler ka laɲini ɲɛ — ni Mediterane jɛɲɔgɔnyaw ye san kɛmɛ filanan laban na Krisita tile ɲɛ. A ka donw tora dɔnnikɛlaw ka faamuyali ye.
A sherd of an urn found in 2004, decorat: Urn dɔ tigɛlen dɔ sɔrɔla san 2004, min masirilen don ni relief appliqué ye ni muso jɔlen ja ye motifw cɛma minnu bɛ kalan tuma caman na i n’a fɔ ɲɔkisɛw, saga, kran ani nɛgɛso. Dɔnnibaaw ye ba ala fɔlɔ dɔ ye a la — dɔw, i n’a fɔ filimu b’a fɔ cogo min na, Kotravai ɲɛbila ye, n’o ye Sangam poyi kɛlɛ ala ye. O ye Tamil Nadu nɛgɛ waati ja ja dɔ ye minnu man ca.
A short illustrated guide for visitors:: Gafe surun jalen dɔ taamabagaw ye: Sangam poyi ye mun ye, u bɛ kulu cogo min na, ani akam ni puram poyi ni dugukoloko duuru bɛ ​​baara kɛ cogo min na.
A silver kasu of Rajendra Chola combinin: Rajendra Chola ka warijɛ kasu min bɛ masakɛ taamasiyɛnw fara ɲɔgɔn kan — Chola jara ni Pandya jɛgɛ ani Chera bow. Rajendra I (1014–1044 K.Ɲ.) ye Chola fanga ta ka taa Ganges ani ka kɔgɔji tigɛ ka taa Azi Saheli-Kɔrɔn fɛ, ani a ka warijɛw b’a jira ko a ye Tamil masafugulan saba bɛɛ kuntigiya ye.

Agriculture remains an important part of: Sɛnɛ tora Tamil Nadu sɔrɔko ni togodala ɲɛnamaya yɔrɔ nafamaba ye. Sɛnɛfɛnba dɔw ye tiga, kɔɔri, shɔ, dugukolonɔn, shɔ, ani shɔ ye, sɛnɛ kɛcogo bɛ danfara ka kɛɲɛ ni dugukolo, sanji, jiko, ani sugu ɲinini ye. Bi sɛnɛkɛlaw bɛ baara kɛ ni laadala dɔnniyaw ni bi fɛɛrɛw faralen ye ɲɔgɔn kan, i n’a fɔ tarakitɛriw, masinw tigɛlanw, kisɛw ɲɛnabɔlenw, jiko pɔnpew, ani dugukolo maracogo. Jibɔ ni jiko fɛɛrɛ wɛrɛw bɛ se ka dɛmɛ don ka jiko gɛlɛyaw ɲɛnabɔ sɛnɛko siratigɛ bɛnnenw na. Sɛnɛkɛlaw fana bɛ gɛlɛyaw sɔrɔ i n’a fɔ sanji min tɛ na tuma bɛɛ, ja, fɛnw musakaw bɛ ka caya, baarakɛlaw dɛsɛ, ani suguw sɔngɔ caman yeli. O la, Tamil Nadu ka sɛnɛko ciyɛn bɛ tariku jan jira, min ye ka ladamu sigida sigida cogoyaw la, ani seko ni dɔnko yiriwali min bɛ bi sɔrɔko ni waati degunw jaabi.
Agriculture was an important source of f: Sɛnɛ tun ye balo, balo ani sɔrɔko baara nafama ye Tamil jamana kɔrɔ la. Sangam sɛbɛnw, minnu bɛ tali kɛ waati la kosɛbɛ san 300 K.Ɲ.–300 K.Ɲ., olu bɛ sɛnɛ sigidaw, foro sɛnɛtaw, waati sanjiko, baganmara ani sɛnɛ baara ɲɛfɔ. Tamil poyikɛlaw ye dugukolo cogoya wɛrɛw siri ɲɔgɔn na ni ɲɛnamaya kɛcogo danfaralenw ye. Marutham dugukolo tun bɛ sɛnɛyɔrɔ nafamaw jira, ɲɔsɛnɛ ni sɛnɛ baara wɛrɛw tun bɛ yɔrɔ minnu na. Sɛnɛkɛlaw tun bɛ sɛnɛfɛnw sugandi ka kɛɲɛ ni dugukolo cogoya ye, sanji hakɛ ani ji sɔrɔcogo. Tiga, shɔ, kɔɔri, shɔ, shɔ ani sesamɛ ye sɛnɛfɛnw ye minnu kofɔlen don Tamil sɛnɛ kɔrɔw ka sɛgɛsɛgɛliw la. Sɛnɛ tun bɛ bɔ hadamadenw ka baara la, baganw ka fanga la, ani sigida lamini cogoyaw dɔnni na. Sɛbɛnni daliluw bɛ hakilina nafamaw di sɛnɛko ɲɛnamaya kan, hali n’u ka kan ka kɔrɔfɔ ka fara fɛnkɔrɔw ni tariku ɲininiw kan.

Ancient and medieval Tamil irrigation sy: Tamil jibɔcogo kɔrɔw ni cɛmancɛla waatiw tun bɛ baara kɛ ni jibɔyɔrɔw ye minnu dilannen don koɲuman walasa ka ji bɔ jidagayɔrɔw la ka taa sɛnɛyɔrɔw la cogo min na, olu kɔlɔsi. Laadalata sɔgɔsɔgɔninjɛ suguya caman sɛbɛnnen bɛ Tamil Nadu, i n’a fɔ madai, madagu, thumpu ani kumizhi. U dilanni tigitigiw n’u ka baarakɛcogo tun tɛ kelen ye. Misali min ka di kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnenya la, o ye kumizhi sigida ye, n’o ye sɔgɔsɔgɔninjɛ kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnen ye min bɛ tali kɛ laadala jibolisira-jiw marali la. U jɔli bɛ dɔnniya waleyali jira ji tansiyɔn, bɔyɔrɔw bilali, girinya ani jɛɲɔgɔnya min bɛ ji marayɔrɔw ni sɛnɛyɔrɔw cɛ. Classical Tamil tradition describes Pala: Tamil kɔrɔlen laada bɛ Palai ɲɛfɔ iko dugukolo min dilannen don ni mara wɛrɛw, kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnenya la Kurinji walima Mullai, bɛ funteni ni ja jugu sɔrɔ — a tɛ kungo ye min bɛ danfara banbali dɔrɔn. A bɛ tali kɛ taama gɛlɛnw na, ji danmadɔw ani dumuni sɔrɔli gɛlɛya. Dumuni minnu bɛ tali kɛ Palai la : shɔ gɛlɛnw i n’a fɔ kambu ni varagu, suman jalenw minnu bɛ taa taama na, sogo jalenw o labɛn sugu bɛ kɛ yɔrɔ minnu na, jiriden jalenw ni dumuniw lajɛlenw, jirisunw ni jirisunw, ani sanko ji. Fɛn min bɛ balo kogow kan, o bɛ daminɛ san kɛmɛ 7nan–9nan na — Pallava batosow kɔnɔ ani Jain kɔdingɛ kɔnɔ Sittanavasal — ka tɛmɛ Chola fresco belebelebaw fɛ Thanjavur ka taa Nayak kogow ja jɛlenw na ani Tanjore panɛriw sanulenw na san kɛmɛda 17nan–19nan na. The agal vilakku was a small lamp, commo: Agal vilakku tun ye lanpan fitinin ye, a tun bɛ dilan ni bɔgɔ walima nɛgɛ ye tuma caman na, min tun bɛ kɛ ka yeelen di so kɔnɔ. A tun bɛ tulu ni fiti dɔ minɛ, o min tun bɛ mana walasa ka tasuma bɔ. Tumu lanpanw tun bɛ kɛ du yeelen gansanw kama ani u jɔyɔrɔ tun bɛ diinɛ seliw ni laadala seliw fana na. U dilacogo nɔgɔman y’u kɛ du kɔnɔfɛnw ye minnu bɛ se ka kɛ.
The ammi was a traditional stone tool us: Ammi tun ye laadala kabakurun baarakɛminɛn ye min tun bɛ kɛ ka tulumafɛnw, mɔni, coco ani fɛn wɛrɛw sɔgɔ. Fɛn minnu tun bɛ kɛ, olu tun bɛ bila kabakurun flakɛlen kan ka u maga ni bolola kabakurun fitinin ye fo ka kɛ fɛnmugu ye. A nafa tun ka bon kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnenya la chutneyw, tulumafɛnw ɲagaminenw ani tobilikɛminɛnw labɛnni na. Ammi tora Tamil laadala tobili taamasyɛn dɔnta ye.
The ancient port of Arikamedu near Puduc: Arikamedu kurunbonkariyɔrɔ kɔrɔ min bɛ Puducherry kɛrɛfɛ, o ye Romɛkaw ka anfɔriw, Arretine bɔgɔdagaw ani gilasi sɔrɔ, o min y’a jira ko jago tun bɛ kɛ Tamil kɔgɔjida ni Romɛkaw ka diɲɛ cɛ tuma bɛɛ ani ko a tun ka ca.
The Arani silk saree originates from Ara: Arani siliki saree bɔra Arani la Tiruvannamalai mara la, Tamil Nadu, mara min lakodɔnnen don a ka siliki-sɛnɛ baara fɛ. Laada la, u bɛ dilan ni siliki jiri ye, o sareew bɛ sɔrɔ kulɛri caman na, u cogoyaw ani u dankan cogoya caman na. U ka dilancogo bɛ daminɛ laadalacogo nɔgɔmanw na ka taa a bila sareew la minnu masirilen don kosɛbɛ, minnu dabɔra seliw ni seliw kama. Arani ka finiko ciyɛn bɛ bɔ dɔnniya kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnenw na jiri labɛnni na, finiko baara, kulɛriw faralen ɲɔgɔn kan, ani finiw dilanni kan. Fɛnɲɛnɛmako ye sigida balo dɛmɛ, wa a ye dɛmɛ don mara in ka finiko sɔrɔko la mɔgɔw ni ɲɔgɔn cɛ. Hali ni Arani siliki dilanni daminɛna san tigitigi min na, o ma jɛya, o laadalakow tora Tamil Nadu bololabaarakɛlaw ka baara nafamaba ye. Arani Silk ye GI ka bonya sɔrɔ san 2008. Bi, Arani sareew bɛ ka nafa sɔrɔ u ka laadala bololabaara la ani u ka dɛmɛ na Ɛndujamana saheliyanfan siliki fini suguya caman na.
The Art of the Lost-Wax: A ka seko ni dɔnko ye Lost-Wax

The best-known of the Chola frescoes, in: Chola ka frescow la min lakodɔnnen don kosɛbɛ, tɛmɛsira min bɛ Alabatosoba ka yɔrɔ senuma lamini na: hakilitigi dɔ, kunsigi bɛ min na, masafugulan don a la ani kamalennin dɔ jɔlen bɛ a kɔfɛ kɛrɛfɛ. Kabini a sɔrɔla, o fila in dɔnna ko Rajaraja I, batoso jɔbaga, n’a ka guru Karuvur Thevar, hali ni dɔnnikɛla dɔw ye jatew kalan cogo wɛrɛ la. A jalen don fresco lakika la lime plastiki ɲiginnen kan, ɲɛda minnu bɛ Chola ja dilanbagaw ka layini hakili sigilen ni hakili sigilen jira.
The Brihadisvara Temple from the air: th: Brihadisvara batoso ka bɔ fiɲɛ na: vimana, da sankanso fila, ani foro kogow ni kɔji minnu b’a lamini.
The Brihadisvara Temple in an early pain: Brihadisvara batoso min bɛ ja fɔlɔ dɔ la
The Brihadisvara Temple, inscriptions, s: Brihadisvara batoso, sɛbɛnniw, jɛgɛw, fɛn dilanni fɛnw ani seko ni dɔnko laada minnu bɛ taa ɲɛ, olu bɛ Thanjavur ka ciyɛn yɔrɔ nafamaw mara.
The Buddha with his hand raised in abhay: Buda n’a bolo kɔrɔtalen don abhaya mudra la, o ye taamasiyɛn ye min b’a fɔ ko “aw kana siran”. Budadiinɛ yiriwara Chola waati Nagapattinam, Rajaraja I ye mɔnikɛyɔrɔ dɔ di Srivijaya masakɛ ma yɔrɔ min na, ani Budadiinɛ ka nɛgɛ kɛmɛ caman filila Chola cogo la.
The cabinets in this wing hold CICT edit: Kabini minnu bɛ nin wulu in kɔnɔ, olu bɛ CICT bɔko minnu bɛ Idylls tan ni Anthologies 8 kɔnɔ. Glasi da dɔ da wuli, ka gafe dɔ sugandi, k’a ɲɛw wuli kalanbaga kɔnɔ. Volume kelen-kelen bɛɛ bɛ se ka telesarse fana walisa ka kalan kɛ.
The capital Rajendra I founded to commem: Faaba Rajendra I ye min sigi senkan walasa k’a ka worodugu kanpaɲi hakili jigin; a ka Shiva batoso belebeleba bɛ yen, dugu fanba tɛ yen.
The cave inscriptions at Mangulam near M: Kɔlɔn sɛbɛnni minnu bɛ Mangulam Madurai kɛrɛfɛ, olu bɛ Tamil-Brahmi sɛbɛn kɔrɔw cɛma. U bɛ Pandya faama Nedunchezhiyan kofɔ ani nilifɛn minnu dira mɔnikɛlaw ma.
The celebrated early Chola king of Patti: Chola masakɛ fɔlɔ selilen Pattinappalai ani Porunaratruppadai, setigi Venni kɛlɛ la sɛbɛnniw kɔnɔ. Laada b’a fɔ ko a ye Kallanai sɔrɔ, o ye diversion weir kɔrɔ ye min bɛ Kaveri cɛtigɛ min tun bɛ ji di delta ma; o jɔli dilanna ani ka fɛn caman Changé san kɛmɛ caman kɔnɔ.
The Chera capital of Sangam poetry and S: Chera faaba min bɛ Sangam poyi ni Silappathikaram. A jɔlen tun bɛ yɔrɔ min na, sɔsɔli bɛ o kan: tarikusɛbɛnbaga caman b’a jira ko Karur bɛ Tamil Nadu, dɔw b’a jira ko Thiruvanchikulam bɛ Kodungallur kɛrɛfɛ Kerala. Kandida fila bɛɛ ye taamasiyɛn ye, ni dakunw ye.
The Chera, Chola, and Pandya dynasties e: Chera, Chola ani Pandya masakɛw kelen-kelen bɛɛ tun bɛ warijɛ bɔ minnu tun bɛ u ka masakɛ taamasiyɛnw kan: bow (Chera), tiger (Chola), ani jɛgɛ (Pandya). Tamil warijɛ fɔlɔ fanba tun bɛ sɔgɔ ni nɛgɛ ye, dɔw tun bɛ kɛ ni warijɛ ni plɔmu ye.
The Chola port at the mouth of the Kaver: Chola kurunbonkarila min bɛ Kaveri da la, o tun bɛ seli kɛ a ka jagokɛlaw, suguw ani kurunw kosɔn.
The complete collection of classical tex: Klasik sɛbɛnw dalajɛlen dafalen : bɔko fɔlɔ sɛbɛnnenw ka bɔ Kural ɲɛfɔli sɛbɛnnen fɔlɔw la, Sangam anthologies, epics and gramar, ani scanned volumes rare — minnu maralen bɛ galasi kɔfɛ ani minnu dabɔra ka kalan.
Klasik sɛbɛnw dalajɛlen dafalen: sɛbɛn bɔlen fɔlɔw, Sangam anthologies, epics, grammaire, ani volumes minnu man ca ka kalan.
The Correction of Faults: Hakilila minnu bɛ yen, olu latilenni
The cultivated fields and river plains,: Sɛnɛyɔrɔw ni bajidabaw, sɔgɔmada fɛ waati bɛɛ. A ka ala ye Vendhan (Indra) ye, a jiri ye marutham ye. A barokun ye oodal ye, muso ni cɛ min filila, o ka kɛlɛ sulking. A mɔgɔw ye sɛnɛkɛlaw ye ɲɔforo nafolotigiw la, masakɛw ka nafolo sɔrɔyɔrɔ.
The Dread of Mendicancy: Siranya min bɛ wele ko Mendicancy
The earliest known Tamil writing, carved: Tamilkan sɛbɛnni fɔlɔ min dɔnna, min jalen don kuluw kɔnɔ ani min sɔgɔlen don bɔgɔdaga kan, ka bɔ Mangulam, Jambai, Pugalur ani Keezhadi.
The earliest Tamil dynastic coins, from: Tamilw ka masaya warijɛ fɔlɔw, minnu bɔra san kɛmɛ labanw lamini na Krisita tile ɲɛ, u fanba ye nɛgɛ ni plɔmu yɔrɔ misɛnninw ye minnu ye kɛnɛ walima bulama ye. Pandya warijɛw bɛ waraba ni jɛgɛ stililen dɔ fara ɲɔgɔn kan; Chola warijɛw bɛ waraba jira, a ka c’a la, waraba walima sow bɛ a la; Chera warijɛw bɛ ni bɛlɛkisɛ ni bɛlɛkisɛ ye. Dɔw b’u bɔbagaw tɔgɔ fɔ Tamil-Brahmikan na, i n’a fɔ Pandya warijɛ minnu bɛ kalan பெருவழுதி (Peruvazhuthi) ani Chera masakɛw Makkotai ani Kuttuvan Kotai ka warijɛ ja warijɛw. Mɔgɔ caman sɔrɔla Amaravathi baji da la Karur, Chera santiri kɔrɔ.
The early Pandya port near the mouth of: Pandya kurunbonkariyɔrɔ fɔlɔ min bɛ Thamirabarani da kɛrɛfɛ, min tɔgɔ bɔra a ka perle mɔni na. Kabini o waati, kɔgɔji Dɔgɔyara, ka dugu in To dugu kɔnɔ.
The eight-armed goddess, her face painte: Ala muso min bolo 8 bɛ a ɲɛda la, n’a ɲɛda ye bulu ye, o jɔlen bɛ misi jinɛ Mahisha kunkolo sanfɛ, npan, bɛlɛkisɛ, bɛlɛkisɛw, disiki ani kala bɛ a bolo, k’a sɔrɔ muso fila bɛ taa a fɛ ni wuluwuluw ye. Tamil laada la a ni Korravai bɛ tali kɛ ɲɔgɔn na, n’o ye Sangam poyi kɛlɛ ala ye min ye se sɔrɔ.
The eri system was a major part of tradi: Eri siratigɛ tun ye laadala jiko ɲɛnabɔli yɔrɔba dɔ ye Tamil Nadu jamana na. Eri ye jibɔlan dilannen ye min dilannen don walasa ka sanji ni dugukolo sanfɛjiw lajɛ ani k’u mara. Sanjiba waati la, ji tun bɛ dalajɛ bɔgɔdaga dɔ kɔfɛ. O kɔfɛ, a tun bɛ se ka bila sɛnɛ kama ni sanji dɔgɔyara. O jidagayɔrɔw nafa tun ka bon kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnenya la yɔrɔw la, baji minnu bɛ falen san caman kɔnɔ, olu tɛ se ka da u kan. Ji maralenw tun bɛ ɲɔsɛnɛ ni sɛnɛfɛn wɛrɛw dɛmɛ, ka sɔrɔ jidagayɔrɔw ni a lamini dugukolow tun ye dugu sɛnɛko yɔrɔ dɔ ye. Mara dɔw la, jidagayɔrɔw tun labɛnna ka tugu ɲɔgɔn na: ji min bɛ bɔ sanfɛ jidagayɔrɔ dɔ la, o tun bɛ se ka taa duguma jidagayɔrɔ la, o bɛ sigidamɔgɔw dɛmɛ u ka baara kɛ ni waati sanjiko ye yɔrɔba dɔ kɔnɔ. Eri tun ka ca ni ji marayɔrɔ ye. O tun ye dugu sigicogo belebele dɔ ye min tun bɛ kɛ sababu ye ka bɔgɔ bɔ tuma bɛɛ, ka dilan ani ka jɛ-ka-baara kɛ. Ni jibolisiraw ladonna ka ɲɛ, u ye dɛmɛ don ka ji bɔnɛ dɔgɔya jibolisiraw fɛ minnu ma kɔlɔsi, wa u tun bɛ ji sɔrɔli ɲɛ ja waatiw la.
The fertile Kaveri valley and delta, hea: Kaveri kɔji ni delta nafama, Chola jamana dusukun yɔrɔ. Marka in jɔlen bɛ Kallanai, diversion weir kɔrɔ min bɛ baji kɛrɛfɛ; mara in yɛrɛ bɛ jɛnsɛn delta kɔnɔ.
The first of the Ten Idylls (Pattuppattu: Idili tan fɔlɔ (Pattuppattu), min dabɔra Nakkeerar fɛ. Nin “poyi ɲɛminɛbaga” in kɔnɔ, batokɛla dɔ min dugawu kɛra Matigi Murugan fɛ, o bɛ ɲininikɛla wɛrɛ ɲɛsin a ma, k’a ka sigiyɔrɔ senuma wɔɔrɔ ɲɛfɔ, n’o ye Arupadai Veedu ye.
The Five Landscapes — Land, Love and Foo: Jamana duuru — Dugukolo, Kanuya ani Dumuni
The Five Landscapes at Table: Jamana duuru minnu bɛ Tabali kan
The Five Landscapes in Verse: Jamana duuru minnu bɛ Vɛrise kɔnɔ
The foods that travelled with Tamil trad: Dumuni minnu tun bɛ taa ni Tamil jago ye — pepinɛri nɛrɛma, sɛnzɛri ani kurkuma ɲininen Ɛndu kɔgɔji cɛma, sesame tulu, jirisun jaggery ani mɔni, ani tiga min tun bɛ kɔgɔjidamɔgɔw ta jɛgɛ ni kɔgɔ musaka la.
The four families of Tamil instruments:: Tamil fɔlifɛnw denbaya naani: dogo — masakɛ murasu, parai, thavil, udukkai ani pambai; ninakili — nadaswaram ni baganw ka fɔlikan; juruw — Sangam bards ni veenai ka yazh; ani nɛgɛ — thalam.
The Gangaikondacholeeswaram Temple and i: Gangaikondacholeeswaram Alabatoso n'a lamini bi, a bɛ ye fiɲɛ fɛ.
The Goddess beneath a Parasol: Ala muso min bɛ Parasol dɔ jukɔrɔ
The Grand Anicut across the Kaveri: Grand Anicut min bɛ Kaveri baji cɛtigɛ
The Grand Anicut at work: water rushing: Grand Anicut bɛ baara la: ji bɛ boli ka tɛmɛ a fiɲɛbɔyɔrɔw fɛ, a jibɔyɔrɔ kan ka taa a fɛ ka don delta siraw la. Ja minnu bɔra sɛbɛnnikɛlan na min bɛ Kallanai kan, n’o dilanna Central Institute of Classical Tamil fɛ.
The great courtyard seen through the pal: Lakɔlisoba min bɛ ye masaso jɔlanw ni a ka jirisunba belebelebaw fɛ.
The heroine of Silappathikaram, who prov: Silappathikaram ka jagokɛla, min y’a cɛ Kovalan ka jalakibaliya jira Pandya masakɛ ɲɛkɔrɔ a kɛlen k’a senkɔni kari: a ta tun bɛ rubiw minɛ, masamuso ka perlew. Sɛbɛnnikɛla sanni ka kɛ tariku mɔgɔ sɛbɛnnen ye, a kɛra tilennenya taamasyɛn ye — wa a bɛ bato iko Pattini ani Kannaki Amman Tamil Nadu, Kerala ani Sri Lanka.
The image of Shiva as Nataraja, Lord of: Shiva ja min ye Nataraja ye, Dɔnkili Matigi, min bɛ dɔn kɛ tasuma bololanɛgɛ kɔnɔ, o ye Chola nɛgɛ suguya ye min bɛ seli kosɛbɛ. A bɛ danni, a lakanani ani a wulicogo diɲɛ kɔnɔko jira.
The Jambai inscription in Villupuram dis: Jambai sɛbɛnni min bɛ Villupuram mara la, o tɔgɔ ye ko “Satiyaputo Atiyan Netuman Anci”, min bɛ Atiyaman kuntigiw ni Satiyaputa cɛ minnu kofɔlen don Ashoka ka sariyaw kɔnɔ.
The Kailasanatha Temple, a Pallava-perio: Kailasanatha batoso, Pallava waati kabakurun batoso, ni batoso misɛnninw bɛ a lamini na.
The kalayam, the everyday Tamil clay pot: Kalaya, o ye don o don Tamil bɔgɔdaga ye. A farikolo lamininen n’a kɔ surun bɛ jiw nɛnɛ ani u ta ka nɔgɔn, wa hali bi kalamaw bɛ fili bɔgɔdaga ka wotoro kan, ka tasuma don duguw ka forow kɔnɔ — o ye jɛɲɔgɔnya ɲɛnama ye ni minɛnw ye minnu sɛgɛsɛgɛra Tamil yɔrɔw la.
The Kallanai, or Grand Anicut, across th: Kallanai, walima Grand Anicut, min bɛ Kaveri kɛrɛfɛ — laada la, a bɛ fɔ ko Chola masakɛ Karikala de don — o jɔra walasa ka baji labɛn ani k’a bila sira wɛrɛ kan ka kɛ jibolisiraw ye. A ye Kaveri delta kɛ Tamil Nadu tiga sɛnɛyɔrɔbaw dɔ ye, wa hali bi a bɛ baara kɛ a ka jiko siratigɛ la. (Aw ye Irrigation room lajɛ walasa ka kunnafoni wɛrɛw sɔrɔ Tamil jiko injiniyɛri kan.)
The Kanchipuram silk saree is one of the: Kanchipuram siliki saree ye Tamil Nadu laadala finiw dɔ ye min bɛ seli kosɛbɛ. A bɔra Kanchipuram, tariku finiko yɔrɔ la, nin saree in tɔgɔ bɔra a ka siliki fini nafama na, a ka zari baara gɛlɛnw na, a dancɛw tɛ kelen ye, ani a ka fɛn dilannenw. Laadalata motifw ye batoso sankansow, pakɔw, mangoro, falenfɛnw ani jateminɛ kɛcogo dɔw ye. Saree bɛ siri ni siliki jiri ye, ni zari jiriw ye minnu ɲɛ ye sanu walima warijɛ ye, olu bɛ dɔ fara finiko nafolo kan. Kanchipuram siliki sareew jɔyɔrɔ ka bon Tamil kɔɲɔw la, diinɛ seliw la, seliw la ani ko kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnen wɛrɛw la. Fɛnɲɛnɛmako bɛ seko caman de wajibiya, kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnenya la ni farikolo, dankan ani pallu faralen don ɲɔgɔn kan ni laadala ɲɔgɔndan fɛɛrɛw ye. Bololabaara in yiriwara mɔgɔw ka bɔnsɔnw kɔnɔ, wa a daminɛ san tigitigi ma sigi sen kan tariku kɔnɔ. Kancheepuram Silk ye Geographical Indication (GI) jate sɔrɔ san 2005. Bi, saree in bɛ Tamil Nadu ka finiko ciyɛn jira, bololabaara seko ni dɔnko, ani laadala finiko sigidaw ka ɲɛnamaya taabolo min bɛ senna.
The Kandangi saree is a traditional cott: Kandangi saree ye laadala fini ye min bɛ kɛ ni bɔgɔ ye min bɛ tali kɛ Chettinad mara la, kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnenya la Karaikudi ani a kɛrɛfɛyɔrɔw. A bɛ Dɔn a ka sɛgɛsɛgɛli ja gɛlɛnw fɛ, a ka sɛrɛkiliw, a dancɛw ni ɲɔgɔn cɛ, ani a kulɛri barikamaw fɛ, i n’a fɔ bilen, mutaridi, oranjɛ ani dugukolo bulama. Laada la, a ka finimugu barikama tun bɛnnen don baara ma tuma bɛɛ, o tun bɛ don o don finiw wajibiyalenw jira. Kandangi finiko bɛ Chettinad mara ka cɛɲi ni finiko dɔnniya danfaralen jira. A cogoyaw n’a kulɛriw faralen ɲɔgɔn kan, o b’a danfara Bɔ Ɛndujamana saheliyanfan saree laada caman wɛrɛw la. O dilanni taabolo ye jiri labɛnni ye, ka jiriw labɛn finimugu kan, ka fini siri, ani ka danw ni finiw dafa. Gofɛrɛnaman bololabaarakɛminɛnw b’a jira ko laada in bɛ yen kabini san 150 ni kɔ, hali n’a daminɛ san tigitigi ma jɛya hali bi. Kandangi sareew ye GI ka bonya sɔrɔ san 2019, u ye dɛmɛ don k’u ka marabolo danbe n’u ka laadala bololabaara dɔn ani k’a mara.
The Kaveri in flood at the anicut: Kaveri ka sanjiba la anicut la
The Kaveri in spate below the Grand Anic: Kaveri in spate ka Grand Anicut jukɔrɔ. Tamil poyikɛlaw ye Chola jamana tanu ko Kaveriw ka jamana, min ka nafolotigiya ma ban abada; Silappatikaram b'a seli iko ɲɔ dan tɛ min na. Anicut y’o bonya in tigɛli kɛ sigida ɲɛnabɔlen ye, wa delta kɛra Tamil jamana ka tiga tasa ye.
The Kaveri rushing through the vents: Kaveriw bɛ boli ka tɛmɛ fiɲɛbɔyɔrɔw fɛ
The Knowledge of Indications: Dɔnniya min bɛ tali kɛ taamasiyɛnw na
The Knowledge of the Council Chamber: Dɔnniya min bɛ Conseil ka so kɔnɔ
The Koorainadu saree is associated with: Koorainadu saree bɛ tali kɛ Koorainadu la Mayiladuthurai kɛrɛfɛ Tamil Nadu. A bɛ tali kɛ kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnenya la furusiri laadala finiw na ani finiw nafa laadalakow la Tamil furu laada la. Laadalata suguyaw ye siliki ni siliki-koton finiw ye, minnu dilannen don ani u dilannenw tɛ kelen ye ka kɛɲɛ ni u cogoya ni u kuntilenna kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnen ye. Saree bɛ fini sirilenw jɔyɔrɔ jira denbaya ka seli nafamaw la ani finiko laadalakow lasegin mɔgɔw ni ɲɔgɔn cɛ. A cogoya, a fini ani a masiricogo bɛ se ka ɲɔgɔn ta, o la, misali kelen-kelen bɛɛ ka kan ka sɛbɛn ka kɛɲɛ n’u jɔcogo yɛrɛ ye sanni k’a miiri ko Koorainadu saree bɛɛ bɛ tugu dilancogo kelen na. O laada in bɔyɔrɔ san tigitigi ma Sìgi kosɛbɛ. Koorainadu sarees tora barokun nafama ye walasa ka jɛɲɔgɔnya sɛgɛsɛgɛ finiw, marabolo danbe, bololabaara, ani seli ɲɛnamaya cɛ Tamil Nadu.
The Kovai Kora cotton saree is associate: Kovai Kora cotton saree bɛ tali kɛ Coimbatore n’a lamini finiko mara la. Saree bɛ cotton sɛnɛni, jiri dilanni, finiko, ani finiko jago nafa jira Tamil Nadu. Kora cotton bɛnnen don don suguya caman ma, i n’a fɔ don o don finiw ani jamalajɛw. Kovai Kora Cotton ye GI ka bonya sɔrɔ san 2008. The Thirubuvanam silk saree originates f: Thirubuvanam siliki saree bɔra Thirubuvanam la Thanjavur mara la Tamil Nadu. A bɛ siliki dilancogo kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnen dɔ jira, bololabaarakɛlaw bɛ siliki fini kulɛrilenw dilan min kɔnɔ, minnu masirilen don ni dancɛw ye minnu dilannen don ani laadalafɛnw. Ka kɛɲɛ ni u dilacogo ye, sareew bɛ se ka kɛ ni fɛn dilannenw ye minnu dilannen don ni fɛn dilannenw ye, u kulɛriw bɛ se ka kɛ fɛn ye min tɛ kelen ye, ani fɛn minnu bɛ kɛ ka fɛnw masiri minnu bɛ bɛn seli ni seli finiw ma. Laada in b’a jira ko mara in ka jɛɲɔgɔnya jan bɛ finiko la ani ka finiko dɔnniyaw lase mɔgɔw ma mɔgɔw ni ɲɔgɔn cɛ. Hali ni a bɔyɔrɔ san tigitigi ma sigi sen kan, Thirubuvanam tora mara tɔgɔ nafama ye Tamil Nadu ka siliki-sɛnɛ ciyɛn kɔnɔ. A ka sareew b’a jira cogo min na finiko yɔrɔ danfaralenw ye cogoya danfaralenw ni tɔgɔba sɔrɔ k’a sɔrɔ u bɛ dɛmɛ don Ɛndujamana saheliyanfan finiw tariku bonya la.

The veenai (Saraswati veena) is one of t: Veenai (Saraswati veena) ye Ɛndujamana saheliyanfan klasiki fɔlifɛnw fɔlifɛnba dɔ ye: jiri rezɔnatɛri belebele, kɔ jan fretted, juruw ani tuning pegs, tuma caman na ni resonator filanan ye. The wooden plough, often drawn by cattle: Lɔgɔdaga min tun bɛ sama tuma caman na baganw walima misiw fɛ, o tun bɛ kɛ ka sɛnɛyɔrɔw lajɔ ani k’u labɛn danni kama. A ka fɛn fɔlɔw tun ye paruthi (cotton) ye, o ye fiɲɛba ye min bɛ siri ka kɛ jiri ye ka siri ka kɛ fini ye; pattu (siliki), min tun bɛ dɔn Azi saheliyanfan finiko laada fɔlɔw la, hali ni fiɲɛ minnu tun bɛ kɛ, olu tun tɛ kelen ye waati ni yɔrɔ la; jiriw kalali i n’a fɔ indigo, minnu kofɔlen don Tamil finiko ɲɛfɔli fɔlɔw kɔnɔ; ani nool (jiri), fiɲɛ min bɛ firi walima ka tigɛli kɛ ka kɛ jiri ye min bɛ to sen na min labɛnnen don finimugu kama.

Tamilw ka laadala sɛnɛ kɛcogo tun ye bololabaarakɛminɛnw ye minnu bɛ ji kɔrɔta i n’a fɔ dagaw, segiw ani minɛn minnu bɛ baara kɛ ni levier ye. Pikota, min bɛ fɔ tuma caman na ko levier systeme balanced, o tun bɛ se ka mɔgɔ dɛmɛ ka ji kɔrɔta ni cɛsiri fitinin ye ka tɛmɛ a tali kan ni bolo ye. Levier minɛn min bɛ kɛ cogoya la, o bɛ baara kɛ ni bere jan ye min bɛ jɔ pivot kan, ni minɛn dɔ sirilen bɛ a dakun kelen na, ka counterweight siri a dakun tɔ kelen na. Baarakɛla bɛ minɛn jigin ji la ka a kɔrɔta ka kɛ ji lankolon ye ka don jibolisira walima foro dɔ kɔnɔ. Tamil sɛbɛnni baara minnu bɛ kɛ, i n’a fɔ Ahananuru, Maduraikanchi ani Silappadikaram, olu kɔnɔ, fɛnw bɛ yen minnu kɔrɔfɔra ko ji kɔrɔtacogo daliluw, ani tariku sɛbɛnniw bɛ dugukolow kofɔ minnu jiginna ni picottah suguya minɛnw ye. O baarakɛminɛnw nafa tun ka bon kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnenya la foro misɛnninw na, nakɔsɛnɛ ani forow minnu bɛ ji sanfɛ.
